Sunnybank



Dear Mr Carter,

Re: Mrs Jenny Perkins Perkines, aged 65 years                                                           Commented [OETONLINE1]: Try to spell the name correctly!



I am writing to request urgent assessment and surgical management for Mrs Perkines who has been
diagnosed with sigmoidal volvulus in our Emergency Department.



Yesterday, Mrs Perkins presented complaining of food poisoning symptoms, including bilious vomiting     Deleted: e
and mild abdominal pain for which fluids, analgesia and metoclopramide were given. Today, her           Deleted: M
symptoms have worsened and appetite decreased. In addition, she had fatigue, dizziness and hiccups
and has experienced constipation for four days.

On examination, Mrs Perkins’s abdomen was tender and bloated for which and no bowel sounds could        Commented [OETONLINE2]: Compound sentence seems
be heard. Although her blood pressure was low, her pulse rate was high. Her abdomen was tympanic on     better here
palpation and the skin was clammy. Despite the fact that her potassium, magnesium and creatinine        Deleted: e
were low, her urea was high. An abdominal x-ray revealed a coffee bean shape mass which indicate a
possible stricture. Due to a diagnosis of a large bowel obstruction, a nasogastric decompression was
conducted, and intravenous fluids and analgesia were commenced. Kindly note, she has Chron’s disease,
had childhood volvulus and has a positive family history of colon cancer.                               Commented [OETONLINE3]: Excellent writing J
